links.note: What you would ask Yama if you were Nachiketa - this concept tells the Katha Upanishad story of Nachiketa persisting with his one question to the god of death. Already linked and correct.
The central ideas of Buddhism - this concept is where the Buddha starts teaching what he had realised, giving ahimsa, sincere inner discipline and the Sangha, which is what the answer sets out.

The saying that not by water is one made pure, though many people may bathe in sacred rivers - this concept quotes it and notes that the chapter singles it out for class discussion because it sets inner purity against ritual bathing.
The central ideas of Jainism - this concept sets out the three principles, ahimsa illustrated by Mahavira's saying, anekantavada and aparigraha, plus the interdependence of all creatures.

Andre Beteille's thought on castes and tribes influencing each other since the beginning of history, and Hinduism being influenced by tribal religions throughout its evolution. Already linked and correct.
Listing popular gods and goddesses of your region with the festivals associated with them is verbatim one of this concept's closing questions.
Listing two or three tribal groups from your region or state and documenting their art and belief systems is verbatim the class activity in this concept's question set.

The seven true-or-false statements - palm-leaf manuscripts, the Vedas as India's oldest texts, ekam sat vipra bahudha vadanti, Buddhism older than the Vedas, Jainism as a branch of Buddhism - are exactly this concept's list. Already linked and correct.
Staging a play with Yama surrounded by several Nachiketas draws entirely on this concept's Nachiketa story and his persistence in questioning. Already linked and defensible, so left alone.
Indian culture likened to an ancient tree with many roots and many branches nurturing a common trunk - this concept's opening figure.
Veda from the Sanskrit vid, meaning knowledge, hence vidya - this concept's etymology. Already linked and correct.
The hymns recited orally rather than written, committed to memory through rigorous training for 100 to 200 generations - this concept's account. Already linked and correct.
The hymns composed in the Sapta Sindhava region - this concept states it while introducing the four Vedas.
UNESCO recognising Vedic chanting as a masterpiece of the oral and intangible heritage of humanity in 2008 - this concept's box. Already linked and correct.
Rishis as male seers or sages and rishikas as female ones - this concept gives both words. Already linked and correct.
Sabha and samiti both referring to a collective gathering or assembly - this concept's few clues about Vedic governance. Already linked and correct.
Brahman as the one divine essence in Vedanta, not to be confused with the god Brahma - this concept's definition, with atman as the sibling term it also defines.
Atman or Self as the divine essence residing in every being and ultimately one with brahman - this concept's gloss.
Sarve bhavantu sukhinah - this concept quotes that prayer and gives the reasoning behind it, that everything in this world is connected and interdependent.
Siddhartha Gautama born in Lumbini, today in Nepal - this concept's opening sentence.
The chariot ride at 29 on which he saw an old man, a sick man and a dead body, and then an ascetic - this concept's four sights, which is what led him to give up palace life.
Enlightenment attained after meditating for many days under a pipal tree at Bodh Gaya, today in Bihar - this concept's account.
Buddha meaning the enlightened or awakened one - this concept's closing gloss.
Avidya, ignorance, and attachment as the source of human suffering - this concept states exactly that as what he realised at Bodh Gaya, and glosses attachment.
Ahimsa generally translated as non-violence but originally meaning non-hurting or non-injuring - this concept's careful distinction. Already linked and correct.
Vardhamana born into a royal family near Vaishali in modern-day Bihar in the early 6th century BCE - this concept's account. Already linked and correct.
Jina meaning conqueror, not of territory or enemies but of ignorance and attachments - this concept's DON'T MISS OUT box on the name.
Aparigraha as non-possession, advising detachment from material possessions and limiting oneself to what is truly necessary - this concept's third principle. Already linked and correct.
The Jataka tales, telling stories of the Buddha's former births and expressing Buddhist values in simple terms - this concept's closing sentences introduce them in those words.

Rohineya the burglar who heard Mahavira's sermon, confessed and became a monk - this concept tells that story and says it illustrates right action and right thinking and that everyone should have a second chance.
A tribe as a group of families or clans sharing a tradition of common descent, a culture and a language - the anthropological definition this concept gives. Already linked and correct.
705 tribes in 2011, about 10.4 crore people - this concept's official figures.

Mountains, rivers, trees, plants, animals and some stones regarded as sacred in folk, tribal and Hindu belief systems alike, because there is consciousness behind all of them - this concept's answer to why the interaction was so natural.
The hymns composed by rishis and rishikas in an early form of the Sanskrit language - this concept's sentence. Already linked and correct.

Anekantavada paired with Jainism is the correct match, and this concept is where anekantavada is defined as the truth having many aspects, alongside aparigraha; brahman and yajna belong to the Vedic concepts the distractors misattribute.
